decisions.reason: The award in 2019 is an early positive signal and, because the probe builds directly on the firm's core tube and system capabilities, management would likely keep this option open.

Although there is no clear market proof yet, it is close to the established geothermal offering and should be relatively inexpensive for a large diversified firm to continue offering while uncertainty resolves.

As a surface technology linked to the geothermal line, it remains strategically connected to the core business and is more likely to be retained as a supporting option than abandoned without clear negative evidence.

A fire-protection steel profile system fits well with the firm's building-systems portfolio, and in a growing market management would usually keep such a close-to-core extension unless results were clearly poor.
The slim steel profile system is a plausible architectural variant within the existing profile business, so the firm would likely continue it while learning about demand rather than exit quickly.
This decorative surface system appears somewhat more niche and easier to prune than the others, but as a near-core product with limited evidence of failure it would still more likely be kept for now.
